newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor CEO says examining other oil deals.
newsitem.headline: Suncor CEO says examining other oil deals.

text.p: Suncor Energy Inc is scouting new long-term deals to supply refiners with output from its oil sands operation to complement one announced on Monday, Suncor Chief Executive Rick George said.
"We're talking to a number of parties about this, particularly in the U.S.," George said in a telephone interview.
"What we're really trying to target is refineries that can run the kind of products we put out and make more money than they make today. Those discussions continue," he said.
Those deals are made easier by the plant's ability to tailor products from the oil sand's plant to the needs of various refiners and markets, he said.
Suncor said earlier today it struck a deal with Koch Oil Co Ltd to supply the refiner with 30,000 barrels a day of light sour crude oil from its expanding oil sands operation.
Suncor said it would start shipping the oil to Koch's refinery in Minnesota when oil sands production hits a targeted 105,000 barrels a day in 1999.
The operation, located north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, is expected to pump out 85,000 barrrels a day of synthetic oil in the second half of this year.
The deal was seen as a building block in boosting output from Suncor's oil sands mine and plant -- Canada's second-largest -- beyond the current target for 1999, George said.
He said earlier this year that Suncor was considering joint ventures or acquisitions of refineries in the U.S. to secure long-term markets for its growing synthetic oil output.
However, George said on Monday that market conditions and the company's ability to secure long-term contracts have taken such a deal off Suncor's priority list.
"That seems more remote today, just because of some of the prices that seem to be out there," he said.

He said the company was in the process of devising plans for expansion of the oil sands plant beyond 105,000 barrels a day and expected to be in a position to provide details on the new project late in the third quarter. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
